title: 听力模拟测试
goal: 完成新闻、长对话和篇章的信息判断。

points.label: 完成新闻主旨与事实判断
完成长对话的信息判断

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲（2016年修订版）

body.p: 听力理解包含短篇新闻、长对话和听力篇章，分别为 7、8、10 题。听力部分共 25 分钟，录音播放 1 遍。
本课程采用四选一题目，通过率为 0.7。

lines.text: A town has reopened a footbridge over its river after repairs that began last spring. The bridge connects a residential street with a park and was closed when an inspection found damage to its wooden surface. Workers replaced the damaged boards and checked the metal supports beneath them. The town also installed new lights at both ends of the bridge. Officials said the lights were added to make the entrances easier to see in the evening. During the closure, walkers used a longer route along the main road. The park itself remained open throughout the work. A local resident who attended the reopening said the bridge made it easier to reach the park on foot. The town will continue to inspect the bridge regularly, particularly after periods of heavy rain. Officials said no changes were made to the river channel. A small sign beside the entrance explains the work and asks visitors to report any damage they notice.

items.stem: What is the report mainly about?
options: A repaired footbridge returning to use
A longer route replacing the bridge
A river channel being moved elsewhere
A residential street closing permanently
items.why: reopened a footbridge after repairs 概括报道的主要事件，即第一项。

items.stem: Why were lights installed at the bridge entrances?
options: To help workers check the supports
To make the entrances easier to see
To close the park during the evening
To replace signs along the main road
items.why: lights were added to make the entrances easier to see in the evening，即第二项。

lines.text: A city library has begun lending small tools to residents as part of a new community service. Members can borrow items such as screwdrivers and hand drills for household projects. The library started the service after receiving requests from residents who needed tools only occasionally. Staff members check each item when it is returned and provide written instructions with it. Borrowers can reserve tools online or ask at the library desk. The loan period is one week, and the tools must be returned to the same branch. The library is also hosting a series of talks about looking after common household items. The first talk will focus on simple furniture maintenance. A library manager said the service could help residents share equipment rather than each buying an item used only a few times. The manager added that the collection would be reviewed after six months to see which tools were most frequently requested. Books and other existing services will remain available as usual.

items.stem: Why did the library introduce tool lending?
options: Staff needed equipment for library repairs.
Residents requested occasional access to tools.
Residents asked for talks on household items.
Members asked to extend all book loans.
items.why: receiving requests from residents who needed tools only occasionally 说明原因，即第二项。

items.stem: What will the library review after six months?
options: The number of branches offering books
The length of every furniture talk
Which tools receive the most requests
How long each tool loan should last
items.why: which tools were most frequently requested 是复查内容，即第三项。

lines.text: A group of students has opened a weekly market for locally grown produce on the grounds of a college. The market brings together growers from nearby communities and takes place every Wednesday afternoon. Organizers said the idea came from a student survey about access to fresh food. Several growers sell vegetables, fruit, and herbs, while a student team provides information about the market. The team does not handle the growers' sales. The college has made an outdoor area available for the event and has agreed to provide an indoor room if the weather is poor. Organizers first planned to hold the market on Fridays, but changed the day after speaking with growers about their delivery schedules. They will collect comments from visitors and sellers during the first term. A spokesperson said those comments would help the group decide whether to extend the market into the following term. The college's usual food shops will continue to operate during market hours. The market began this week with six growers taking part.

items.stem: What prompted the students to organize the market?
options: A survey about access to fresh food
A decision to close college food shops
A request from local growers
A college offer of an outdoor area
items.why: a student survey about access to fresh food 是活动构想的来源，即第一项。

items.stem: Why did organizers change the planned day?
options: The indoor room was unavailable on Fridays.
Visitors requested a weekend event instead.
They considered growers' delivery schedules.
The college closed all food shops on Wednesdays.
items.why: changed the day after speaking with growers about their delivery schedules，即第三项。

items.stem: What will the organizers use comments to decide?
options: Whether to replace growers with students
Whether to continue the market next term
Whether to close the college's food shops
Whether to hold the market on Fridays
items.why: comments would help ... decide whether to extend the market into the following term，即第二项。

audio.intro: Listen to a conversation between Alex and Nina.

lines.text: Hi Nina. Have you heard that our department wants to hold a book exchange next month?
Yes, Alex. I offered to help organize it, but we're still deciding where to hold it.
The entrance hall is easy to find. Would that work?
We considered it, but people pass through there between classes. Tables might block the way.
What about the room beside the student cafe? It's larger and has a separate entrance.
I checked yesterday. It's free on Thursday afternoon, though the cafe itself will be closed for maintenance.
That sounds suitable. How will people know what books to bring? I have some novels at home, and a few classmates mentioned that they have textbooks from last year.
We'll accept books in good condition. Textbooks and novels are both welcome, but we cannot take magazines because we have limited storage. We also need room to sort the books before visitors arrive.
We should explain that on the notices. I can draft one and send it to you tonight.
Thank you. Please include the room and time, but leave the collection date blank until I confirm it with the department office.
Will visitors need to bring a book in order to take one?
No. We want everyone to be able to participate. Any books left afterward will go to the community reading room.
I'll prepare the notice and wait for your message about the collection date.
I'll contact the office tomorrow morning and let you know as soon as it replies.

items.stem: Why was the entrance hall rejected?
options: The cafe needed it for maintenance.
The book tables could obstruct passing students.
The department office had reserved it for Thursday.
The room was too far from the student cafe.
items.why: people pass through 和 Tables might block the way 说明原因，即第二项。

items.stem: What is known about the room beside the cafe?
options: It is free on Thursday afternoon.
It will be closed for maintenance.
It has no separate entrance.
It cannot hold any book tables.
items.why: It's free on Thursday afternoon 指该房间可用，即第一项。

items.stem: Why will the exchange not accept magazines?
options: Magazines are rarely in good condition.
Visitors must bring only textbooks.
The department has limited storage.
The reading room will not take magazines.
items.why: cannot take magazines because we have limited storage 给出原因，即第三项。

items.stem: What will Alex do next?
options: Confirm the collection date with the office
Deliver leftover books to the reading room
Reserve the cafe for a maintenance meeting
Draft a notice and wait for the collection date
items.why: I'll prepare the notice and wait for your message 说明 Alex 的任务，即第四项。

audio.intro: Listen to a conversation between Sara and Daniel.

lines.text: Daniel, I saw your message about the student film evening. Are you still looking for a place to show the films?
Yes, Sara. We wanted the main theater, but it is being painted that week.
The lecture room in the arts building has a screen. Has anyone checked its sound equipment?
I did. The speakers work, but the room has fewer seats than the theater.
Could we show the same films twice? That would give more people a chance to attend. Some people might also find one time more convenient than the other.
That's possible. The room is available at six and again at eight. We could ask people to reserve a seat for either showing. That would help us keep each group within the room's capacity.
I'll make a simple reservation form. What information should it request?
A name, an email address, and the preferred showing should be enough. We don't need student numbers because guests from outside the college are welcome.
Should we include a question about which film people want to see?
The same four films will be shown at both times, so that question isn't necessary.
All right. When would you like the form ready?
By Friday, please. I'll confirm the room booking tomorrow and send you the exact address for the form.
I'll prepare the form today and add the address when you send it.
Great. After the bookings are confirmed, I'll ask the film makers to introduce their work at each showing.

items.stem: Why is the main theater unavailable?
options: Its screen has stopped working.
It is being painted that week.
Its seats are reserved for guests.
It is hosting the same four films.
items.why: the main theater ... is being painted that week，即第二项。

items.stem: Why does Sara suggest two showings?
options: The lecture room has fewer seats.
The four films require different screens.
The sound equipment works only at eight.
The film makers cannot attend at six.
items.why: fewer seats 后 Sara 建议播放两场，使更多人能够参加，即第一项。

items.stem: Why are student numbers unnecessary on the form?
options: Every film maker is a student.
The room has no reservation system.
Guests from outside the college may attend.
The form will be completed after the event.
items.why: guests from outside the college are welcome 说明不要求学号，即第三项。

items.stem: What will Daniel send Sara after confirming the booking?
options: The names of the four film makers
The list of visitors at each showing
The times of the two film showings
The exact address of the lecture room
items.why: send you the exact address for the form 对应第四项。

lines.text: A small museum recently changed the way it presents objects from its local collection. Previously, each object was displayed with a label giving its name and date. Staff noticed that visitors often looked at the objects briefly and then moved on. The museum decided to add short accounts of how some objects had been used in daily life. For example, a sewing box now appears beside a description of the materials it held and the work for which they were used. The original date and name remain on the label. The accounts were prepared from records already held by the museum, rather than from assumptions about the objects. After the changes, staff observed that some visitors spent more time at the cases with the new accounts. The museum has not concluded that the accounts alone caused the change. A new school program began during the same period, and it may also have affected visitor behavior. Staff plan to ask visitors what they notice and to compare observations over a longer period. They also want to find out whether the extra text is easy to read from the space in front of each case. The aim is to make the collection easier to understand while keeping the information reliable. The museum will adjust the displays if the feedback shows that important details are difficult to find.

items.stem: What change did the museum make to some displays?
options: It removed the names and dates from labels.
It replaced all objects with written records.
It added accounts of the objects' everyday uses.
It moved the collection into a school building.
items.why: add short accounts of how some objects had been used in daily life 对应第三项。

items.stem: Why does the speaker mention the sewing box?
options: To give an example of an object with an added account
To show that all sewing records had been lost
To show how labels looked before the change
To describe an object made for the new school program
items.why: For example 引出缝纫盒及其使用说明，作为新增内容的实例，即第一项。

items.stem: What can be inferred about the observed increase in time at some cases?
options: It proves that every visitor read every account.
It may have more than one explanation.
It occurred before the accounts were added.
It was caused by the new accounts alone.
items.why: 依据是 has not concluded that the accounts alone caused the change，同期还有新的 school program。停留时间变长可能不止一个原因，即第二项。

lines.text: When a neighborhood garden began sharing its tools, members discovered that keeping a record was as important as choosing the tools themselves. At first, anyone could take a tool from the shed and return it later. The arrangement was convenient, but members sometimes arrived to find that the item they needed was already in use. The group introduced a paper sheet beside the shed door. A member wrote the name of the tool and the expected return time before taking it. At the end of the first month, the sheet helped members see when popular tools might be available. It did not, however, guarantee that a tool would be returned on time. One member suggested an online calendar, while another preferred the paper sheet because it could be read without a phone. The group decided to keep the sheet and add a space for a contact name. That way, a member waiting for an item could ask the borrower about the return time. The tools remained available to all members, and no fee was introduced. The group also agreed to check the condition of the tools at a monthly meeting. The record therefore served a particular purpose: it made current borrowing visible. It did not replace communication between members or the need to maintain the tools. The garden plans to review the system again after the next growing season.

items.stem: What problem led the garden to introduce a record sheet?
options: Tools were often returned in poor condition.
Members sometimes found needed tools already in use.
The garden had stopped lending every tool.
The online calendar had charged a fee.
items.why: item they needed was already in use 是设置记录表之前的问题，即第二项。

items.stem: Why did the group add a contact name to the sheet?
options: To allow members to ask borrowers about returns
To charge borrowers for each use of a tool
To replace the monthly check of tool condition
To prevent members without phones from borrowing
items.why: could ask the borrower about the return time 说明增加联系人的目的，即第一项。

items.stem: What does the speaker imply about the record sheet?
options: It guarantees that every tool returns on time.
It makes all communication between members unnecessary.
It helps show borrowing but has limits.
It proves that online calendars cannot be used.
items.why: made current borrowing visible，同时 did not replace communication，支持第三项。

lines.text: A college group wanted to improve the signs directing visitors to its annual exhibition. In the previous year, the exhibition had been held in a room near the main entrance. This year, building work meant that the event moved to a room on the other side of the campus. The group put a map on its website and placed signs at several entrances. On the morning of the event, two volunteers stood near the main gate and watched how visitors used the signs. They noticed that some people paused at the first sign but then walked toward the old exhibition room. The volunteers moved a second sign closer to the point where the path divided. After that, they saw fewer people take the path toward the old room during the period they observed. The group regarded this as useful information, but it did not count every visitor throughout the day. Later, the volunteers asked several visitors whether the map had helped. Some said they had used it before arriving, while others had relied on the signs at the gate. The group kept notes on both types of response. For the next exhibition, it plans to check the route before the event and make sure that signs are visible where visitors must choose a direction. The experience showed the value of observing how information is used, as well as preparing it in advance.

items.stem: Why did the exhibition move to a different room?
options: The main gate had closed for the day.
Building work affected the earlier location.
The website map was no longer available.
Visitors requested a smaller exhibition.
items.why: building work meant that the event moved 给出原因，即第二项。

items.stem: What did the volunteers do after noticing visitors take the old route?
options: They moved a sign nearer the path division.
They removed the map from the website.
They closed the path to the old room.
They moved the exhibition back to its old room.
items.why: moved a second sign closer to the point where the path divided，即第一项。

items.stem: What did the volunteers observe after moving the sign?
options: All visitors used the website map.
Every visitor immediately found the new room.
Fewer observed visitors took the old path.
More visitors went to the former exhibition room.
items.why: saw fewer people take the path toward the old room during the period they observed，即第三项。

items.stem: What is the main point of the passage?
options: An online map always replaces signs at a gate.
Visitors should attend exhibitions near the main entrance.
Moving an exhibition removes the need for directions.
Observing visitors can help improve directions.
items.why: the value of observing how information is used 概括故事说明的观点，即第四项。
